notes: Pipelinq spec REQ language is heterogeneous: ~14 specs use legacy '### REQ-XXX-NNN:' IDs while ~22 specs use the OpenSpec '### Requirement: <title>' canonical form. Used the broader regex `^### (Requirement:|REQ-|[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9])` for inventory.
Effective REQ inventory: ~563 REQs across 37 specs (median 14 per spec).
37 specs but no `status: redirect` / `status: deprecated` / `status: moved` headers; 13 specs marked `status: draft` and 1 each `partial` — these specs' REQs were still classified normally.

Existing @spec annotations cover only 4 capabilities end-to-end: callback-management, skill-routing, task-background-jobs, activity-timeline. The other ~33 specs have zero file-header annotations. ~95% of lib/ is un-annotated despite having matching REQs.

Several large capability-aligned services (NotificationService, KennisbankService, IcpConfigService, MetricsRepository, EmailSyncService, ProspectDiscoveryService, AutomationService, QueueService) are Bucket 1 with high confidence but lack any @spec tags — they are the highest-value targets for `/opsx-annotate`.

Bucket 3b is heavy (80+ unimplemented REQs). Many are V1/Enterprise tier in draft specs (klantbeeld-360, pipeline-insights, product-catalog-quoting, contactmomenten-rapportage, kcc-werkplek). Many UI-heavy REQs ship in src/*.vue rather than lib/ and would only surface in a Vue-side coverage scan.
terugbel-taakbeheer overlaps semantically with callback-management — its REQs are draft and may be redundant; consider archive vs merge.
register-i18n and product-service-catalog deliver via OR schema definitions + JSON i18n files (not PHP code) — their REQs surface as 3b in a PHP-only scan but are not necessarily 'never implemented'.
Bucket 2b is empty — every lib/ file maps cleanly to a capability owner, which is a good sign for the spec taxonomy.
Bucket 2a is small (10 methods, 2 clusters) because most private helpers were resolvable to a Bucket 1 caller via Pass B inheritance.
No forbidden patterns, direct SQL, or SPDX/license header gaps found — Bucket 4 is purely about missing @spec tags.
